en: The Philippine eagle, the national bird, features a distinctive shaggy crest and primarily hunts flying lemurs in Mindanao's forests.
Sampaguita, the national flower of the Philippines, is a fragrant white jasmine scientifically named Jasminum sambac.
The South Sea pearl, produced by the Pinctada maxima oyster found in Palawan, is the national gem of the Philippines.
Filipino scientist Gregorio Zara invented the two-way radio telephone in 1938 and developed the physical law of kinetic energy.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spanish colonial rule on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite.
Jose Rizal wrote the influential novels Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose the abuses of the Spanish colonial government.
The legislative branch of the Philippine government, called the Congress, is divided into the Senate and the House of Representatives.
Under the Philippine Constitution, every citizen has the right to suffrage, allowing them to vote in national and local elections.
The Igorot people of the Cordillera Administrative Region built the ancient Banaue Rice Terraces by carving mountains into giant staircases.
Filipino and English are the two official languages of the Philippines, alongside over a hundred regional languages like Cebuano.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño through a rhythmic two-step forward and one-step backward dance.
The Filipino value of bayanihan is traditionally demonstrated when community members work together to carry a nipa hut to a new location.
